units: PTVS package is described as trajectory-admissibility monitoring and LBR telemetry feeding MRAT.
EnvironmentObservation stores input, expected output, and metadata.
TrajectoryEvaluation stores predicted/observed outputs, residual, and admissibility.
Base environment maintains observation history and requires subclasses to implement observe.
Default evaluation computes residual and admissibility and returns TrajectoryEvaluation.
Default residual is absolute numeric difference; non-numeric domains must override or trigger ValueError.
Default admissibility requires exactly zero residual.
collect_observation calls observe and appends to history.
Exact-zero default admissibility is stricter than PTVSAnalyzer's tolerance-based admissibility, and no source-level reconciliation specifies which rule governs a benchmark.
No concrete subclass of PTVSEnvironment appears on the frozen surface.
TrajectoryRecord stores observable predicted/observed outputs, admissibility, residual, and metadata.
Analyzer defaults tolerance to 1e-6 and stores trajectory records.
Evaluates one prediction, computes residual if absent, marks admissible when residual <= tolerance, and appends record.
Supports scalar absolute error and equal-length list elementwise absolute-error sum; unequal list length returns infinity.
LBR is invalid record count divided by stored trajectory count; empty state returns zero.
Returns mean stored residual or zero when empty.
Analyzer can clear state and export trajectory count, invalid count, LBR, and mean residual.
Analyzer computes LBR over internally stored trajectories only; no sampling/independence semantics are specified.
Residual aggregation for vectors is scale-dependent and not normalized by dimension.
REE package exports REEEngine as gated representation expansion primitive.
REEDecision records expansion authorization, textual reason, expected gain, and representation cost.
REE controller defaults saturation_threshold=0.05 and minimum_gain_margin=0.
Saturation is implemented as absolute difference between baseline_error and compressible_error <= threshold.
Expansion is authorized only when both saturation and benefit conditions hold; otherwise rejected with a reason.
expand simply applies a supplied transformation to a supplied representation; it does not enforce prior authorization.
The code consumes externally supplied compressible_error, expected_future_gain, and representation_cost; it does not estimate these quantities.
Authorization and transformation execution are not coupled by state, so callers can invoke expand without an evaluate approval.
